title: Advanced Props Patterns
description: Learn default props, prop types, spread attributes, and children prop.

data.text: Now that you understand the basics, let's explore advanced prop patterns that make components more flexible and robust.
You can provide default values for props using default parameters. This ensures your component works even when a prop isn't provided.

data.title: Default Props

data.text: The `children` prop allows you to pass content between the opening and closing tags of a component. This is useful for layout components.

data.title: Using Children

data.text: You can spread an object's properties as props using the spread operator. This is useful when you have many props or want to pass them through.

data.title: Spread Attributes

data.text: A render prop is a prop that is a function. It allows a component to share its logic with other components.

data.title: Render Props
When to Use Render Props
data.text: Render props are powerful but can lead to deeply nested code. In modern React, custom hooks are often a cleaner alternative for sharing logic.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use default props for optional values
Spread attributes simplify passing multiple props
Render props share logic between components
data.takeaway: These patterns make your components more flexible. Let's see how to compose components together.
